Decisive historical source check: PHP5.6.25 ext/mcrypt/mcrypt.c zero-PADS nonaligned ciphertext before ECB/CBC decrypt and returns the rounded-length buffer. It does NOT hard-reject as the C port does. Worker has frozen the tag source SHA256340fa4d3282823c7072c820704e0e544f0d863b12641a3b748d99cd9d3d7956d; php_mcrypt_do_crypt lines1299-1305 round/allocate/zero-fill/copy, lines1320-1325 decrypt and return data_size. Official source link: https://github.com/php/php-src/blob/php-5.6.25/ext/mcrypt/mcrypt.c . Root full source review still follows. Application-level tools4noobs trimming remains unknown. The new decrypted last block is arbitrary-looking plaintext, not necessarily trailing NULs.

This suggests a CHEAP proof extension rather than a target rerun. Planned saved-result analysis, before measurement: for each legacyRA READY ECB/CBC block row, the first544 decrypted bytes P are unchanged by appending ciphertext zeros to a546-byte input, under the same ECB/CBC key/IV/primitive convention. Only the new last block changes. Let Q=P.rstrip(NUL). Every possible padded-buffer decryption, with or without trailing-NUL stripping, must begin with Q. Therefore D(output)>=D(Q), and its length lies between len(Q) and the padded length552/560/576. Compare that lower bound against the maximum frozen occupancy cutoff over the entire allowed length interval. If the bound exceeds that maximum, we can close this small-byte-alphabet screen for ALL possible final blocks without computing any new target decryptions.

I have delegated only the proof/control preparation in `coverage/ra_padded_tail_occupancy_bound/` so far. First we will check the lemma with exhaustive small-alphabet prefix/tail controls. Then root will authorize a single read-only pass over the3,312 affected saved rows after sharing the frozen source. No target crypto or keysweep. This covers an explicit fixed-prefix model; it does not assert that historical key derivation or IV handling matches our engines.

Separately, the strict-C-port filter is already measured and root review is underway: it removes3,312 READY block ECB/CBC labels (not the stream-primitive mode aliases), leaving8,388 labels/5,139 unique outputs/minD211/0flags. That filter is C-port compatibility only, and cannot stand in for the PHP behavior just found.
